solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Mount or fasten a bath with ring (8)

annotation.surface: Instructions for fitting out a bathroom: mount the bath or fasten it with a ring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a DIY verb, but it is the noun: Mount Pinatubo is a volcano in the Philippines.
annotation.definitionFit: Pinatubo is a mountain, a volcano on Luzon that erupted in 1991.

entries.clue: Stationery item obtained from secretary with a piece extracted (9)

blocks.note: a = per, as in 'ten pounds a head'
a clip is a piece cut out of a film or article

annotation.surface: A secretary loses part of something and it turns into an office supply.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A' is not kept as a letter here: it means PER. 'With a piece extracted' reads like a deletion instruction, but nothing is removed; the phrase supplies PER and CLIP.
annotation.definitionFit: Stationery covers the small supplies of a desk and office, and a bent-wire clip for holding sheets together is a standard one.

entries.clue: Observed having escaped hit squad? (7)

blocks.note: iced is gangland slang for killed; the question mark warns the answer must be split in two

annotation.surface: A gangland target who got away from the hitmen but was spotted.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic, as the question mark warns: read the answer as NOT ICED, where to ice someone is underworld slang for murdering them.
annotation.definitionFit: Noticed and observed both mean saw.

entries.clue: Go for the King’s Head, perhaps, turning up drunk to drink (4,2)

definitions.text: Go for the King’s Head, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: a sot is a drunkard; turned up, SOT reads TOS

annotation.surface: Deciding whether to head to a pub called the King's Head, having turned up drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: The King's Head looks like a pub, which suits the drinking; here it is the monarch's head on a coin, and calling heads is one go at a coin toss.
annotation.definitionFit: A toss-up is a coin toss, and calling for the head is one way of taking part.

entries.clue: Reserves unlikely attraction for Reading people (9)

blocks.note: a tall story is an unlikely one

annotation.surface: A strange draw for the people of Reading, the English town.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Reading look like the town in Berkshire; it is just people who read. Capitals at the start of a word may always be ignored.
annotation.definitionFit: A bookstall draws people who like reading.

entries.clue: Man snubbed sullen young woman (6)

indicators.note: a snub nose is short, so a snubbed word loses its end

annotation.surface: A man gives a moody young woman the cold shoulder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' looks like the man's rudeness to the woman; it docks the last letter of the word after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Crosswords use a first name as a definition by example of 'man'; Dougal is a Scottish boy's name, familiar from the dog in The Magic Roundabout.

entries.clue: 23 maybe to become less (4,3)

definitions.note: '23 maybe' is a noun, a nap, while DROP OFF is a verb: it is the act that brings one about.

blocks.note: 23 across is a short sleep, and this is what you do to fall into one
to decline or fall away, as sales or numbers do

annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points at 23 across, CATNAP; dropping off is what you do to take one.
annotation.definitionFit: Dropping off is nodding off for a nap, and also falling away in number.

entries.clue: Japanese warrior mostly in uniform twice bloodied, not wounded (9)

indicators.note: most of the word: the last letter goes
the warrior goes inside the pair of Us
uniform's letter U is used two times

blocks.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A ninja comes through two bloody fights without a scratch.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer contradicts the gory surface: the warrior sits between two Us, and 'bloodied' only supplies the colour RED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who comes out of a fight with no harm to their body has escaped without a wound.

entries.clue: Some female NCO near town in France (7)

indicators.note: only some of the letters that follow are used

annotation.surface: A woman sergeant is posted near a French town.
annotation.walkthrough: Alençon is in Normandy, famous for its lace; the cedilla disappears in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: Alençon is a town in north-west France.

entries.clue: Smooth caress? (3)

blocks.note: glib, slick, too readily produced, as of an answer or excuse
a light tap with the flat of the hand, as given to a dog

annotation.walkthrough: 'Smooth caress' reads as one gentle touch, but it is two definitions, one an adjective and one a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Pat means glib or smooth, and it is also a gentle tap.

entries.clue: One’s movement on track: replacement for old women’s lib (10)

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a new order

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old

annotation.surface: A political slogan: a modern movement to replace the old women's lib.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Movement' belongs to the surface's politics as in the women's movement; in the definition it is travel. A snowmobile runs on caterpillar tracks.
annotation.definitionFit: A snowmobile is a vehicle that moves on a track instead of wheels.

entries.clue: Playground belonging to us, source of enjoyment — and of help? (8)

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: the rec is a recreation ground

annotation.surface: Our local park, a place of fun and of help to the community.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Source' works twice: 'source of enjoyment' gives E, and '— and of help' reads on from it, a recourse being a source of help.
annotation.definitionFit: Having recourse to something means turning to it when in trouble, so the word names a source of assistance or aid.

entries.clue: End protest (6)

blocks.note: an aim or purpose, as in 'the end in view'
a verb here: to raise an objection

annotation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a call to stop protesting; the two words are separate definitions, a noun and a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Object means an aim, and also means to protest.

entries.clue: Centre for leisure — and for schooling on top (4)

indicators.note: in an across clue, O placed on LID comes after it

blocks.note: the centre of SCHOOLING, its fifth of nine letters; 'Centre' is borrowed from the definition

annotation.surface: A place that serves both for relaxing and, above all, for lessons.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Centre' does double duty: 'Centre for leisure' is the definition, and 'and for schooling' asks for the centre of SCHOOLING too.
annotation.definitionFit: A lido is a public outdoor swimming pool, a place of leisure.

entries.clue: One in mood smashed up vault (5,4)

indicators.note: broken into pieces and rebuilt

annotation.surface: Someone in a temper wrecks a vault.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smashed up' sounds like a violent mood, and a vault could be a leap or a strongroom; here it is a curved roof.
annotation.definitionFit: In architecture a vault is an arched roof, and a dome is a vault turned on its axis; Russian churches wear bulbous ones shaped like onions.

entries.clue: Second dismissal having unwanted effect (10)

blocks.note: to second a motion is to back it

annotation.surface: Sacking someone a second time turns out badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number, but it is the verb, to support.
annotation.definitionFit: A plan that is backfiring is having the opposite effect to the one wanted.

entries.clue: Eking out, retaining fodder, in critical position (5,4)

indicators.note: the letters of EKING are put out of order
the anagram holds FEED inside it

annotation.surface: A farmer stretching out the animal feed is in a precarious state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fodder' is not anagram fodder here: it is the thing kept whole, FEED, sitting inside the jumbled EKING.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom 'on a knife edge' describes a tense, precarious moment when things could go either way, like something balanced on a blade.

entries.clue: English banker to polish off beef sandwiches (5,4)

indicators.note: GROUSE holds EAT inside like bread round a filling

blocks.note: to beef and to grouse both mean to complain
to polish off food is to eat it

annotation.surface: An English banker finishes off his beef sandwiches.
annotation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is often a river, something with banks. The Great Ouse flows through East Anglia to the Wash.
annotation.definitionFit: The Great Ouse is an English river, and rivers have banks.

entries.clue: Still unwell at home, visited by nurse giving drug (10)

indicators.note: PIC has EN come inside it

blocks.note: a still is a photograph, a pic; split P…IC

annotation.surface: A patient still sick at home gets a nurse's visit and some medicine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb for the ongoing illness; it is a noun, a still photo or PIC.
annotation.definitionFit: Penicillin was the first antibiotic, found by Alexander Fleming in mould in 1928, and is still a widely prescribed medicine.

entries.clue: Short appeal in support of test case (7)

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter
in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so PLE goes after EXAM

annotation.surface: A brief legal appeal backing a test case in court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Test case' reads as one legal phrase; it splits, with 'test' in the wordplay and 'case' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'a case in point' and 'an example' both mean a single instance chosen to illustrate something general.

entries.clue: Better way to act: on impulse, ultimately (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, E placed on IMPROV follows it
ultimately means in the end, so take the letter that ends the word

annotation.surface: Advice that acting on impulse is the better way in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' is the verb here, to improve on something, not the comparative adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Better as a verb means to make something superior, as in 'bettering a record', which is exactly what improving does.

entries.clue: Nobleman expected to receive king (4)

indicators.note: to receive a guest is to take them in, so DUE takes K inside it

annotation.surface: A nobleman is expected to host the king.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a royal visit, which is why the nobleman and king sit comfortably together.
annotation.definitionFit: Dukes head the British peerage, above marquesses, earls, viscounts and barons, so a duke is the top rank of titled aristocrat.

entries.clue: Instrument in Junkie Blues lies neglected in odd places (7)

indicators.note: the 1st, 3rd, 5th… letters are ignored, leaving the even ones

blocks.note: jUnKiE bLuEs LiEs: the even letters

annotation.surface: A song called Junkie Blues is a lie about neglect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd places' sounds like strange locations; it means odd-numbered letter positions.
annotation.definitionFit: The ukelele, more often spelt ukulele, is a small four-stringed guitar.

entries.clue: Ease with which daughter’s restrained until nightfall? (3-3)

indicators.note: ALLAY holds D in check inside it

blocks.note: to allay = to ease; split ALL…AY

annotation.surface: A daughter is kept in easily until dark.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'until nightfall' is loose for ALL-DAY: from morning until night.
annotation.definitionFit: Something all-day lasts the day through, until night falls.

entries.clue: Accountant returned to blow the rest of the kitty? (6)

indicators.note: the word that follows is turned back

blocks.note: to blow is to pant, breathe hard; returned, PANT reads TNAP

annotation.surface: An accountant comes back and fritters away what is left of the shared fund.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' and 'rest' pose as money and remainder; the definition is a pun, a cat's rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short sleep, the sort of rest a kitty takes.

entries.clue: Set criminal on underworld! (8)

indicators.note: in an across clue, BENT placed on HELL comes after it

annotation.surface: An order to unleash a crook on the gangland underworld.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like an instruction; it is the adjective, determined, as in 'set on winning'.
annotation.definitionFit: Set can mean determined, as in 'set on going', and hellbent describes someone recklessly determined to do something whatever the cost.

entries.clue: Suggested getting hammered after getting paid (10)

indicators.note: after means following in position, so POUNDED is written following PRO

blocks.note: a professional is someone who gets paid

annotation.surface: Someone got drunk once the wages came in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' suggests drunk after payday; it means beaten, POUNDED.
annotation.definitionFit: To propound an idea is to put it forward, to suggest it.

entries.clue: Bird’s leg bone skinned (3)

indicators.note: the outer layer, first and last letters, comes off

blocks.note: the femur is the thigh bone

annotation.surface: A cook skinning a bird's leg down to the bone.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a butcher's job on a drumstick; the bird is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

entries.clue: Problem in photography studied and indeed spoken of (3,3)

indicators.note: the words are to be said aloud

annotation.surface: A photography student studies a known flaw.
annotation.walkthrough: Past-tense READ is said like RED, which is how 'studied' reaches the colour.
annotation.definitionFit: Red-eye is the red glare in subjects' eyes caused by a camera flash.

entries.clue: Converting current to energy, entirely transformed material (8)

indicators.note: one letter is changed into another
the new letter it becomes
the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
E is the symbol for energy
ENTIRELY with its I swapped for E

annotation.surface: Physics notes on converting electric current into energy.
annotation.walkthrough: The physics symbols do the work: current I becomes energy E inside ENTIRELY before the jumble. Terylene is a British brand name for polyester.
annotation.definitionFit: Terylene is a synthetic polyester fabric.
